headline_marked: Court [[scraps order to exhume actor Salman Shah's body]] nearly 30 years after death
headline: Court scraps order to exhume actor Salman Shah's body nearly 30 years after death
summary: A Dhaka court has cancelled the directive to dig up the remains of the legendary film star, following an application from the actor's maternal uncle.
details: A Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate court has cancelled an order to exhume the body of film star Chowdhury Mohammad Shahriar Emon, popularly known as Salman Shah, nearly 30 years after his death.
The directive was passed on Tuesday by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jewel Rana, following an application filed by the plaintiff in the case.
The application to scrap the exhumation order was filed by Mohammad Alamgir Kumkum, the maternal uncle of the deceased actor and the plaintiff in the case.
The court had originally granted permission for the exhumation on May 24, which became public on June 10, following a request from CID Inspector Ziaul Morshed.
The CID had argued that exhuming the body was necessary to complete an inquest report and review postmortem findings for a proper investigation into the murder case.
The murder case had been filed with Ramna Police Station 29 years after the incident occurred.
caption:
A Dhaka court has stopped the exhumation of legendary actor Salman Shah's remains nearly 30 years after his death.

A Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate court has cancelled an order to exhume the body of film star Chowdhury Mohammad Shahriar Emon, popularly known as Salman Shah, nearly 30 years after his death.

The directive was passed on Tuesday by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jewel Rana, following an application filed by the plaintiff in the case.

The application to scrap the exhumation order was filed by Mohammad Alamgir Kumkum, the maternal uncle of the deceased actor and the plaintiff in the case.

The court had originally granted permission for the exhumation on May 24, which became public on June 10, following a request from CID Inspector Ziaul Morshed.

The CID had argued that exhuming the body was necessary to complete an inquest report and review postmortem findings for a proper investigation into the murder case.

The murder case had been filed with Ramna Police Station 29 years after the incident occurred.
